subject: ela
skillName: Develop and strengthen writing through planning, revising, editing
intro: Good writers improve their work in stages: they plan before they write, revise to make ideas clearer and better organized, and edit to fix spelling, capitalization, punctuation, and grammar. For each item, read the short sentence or action and complete the single task. Remember: revising changes ideas, content, and organization, while editing only fixes surface conventions.

items.prompt: Read the action: "Before writing, Jordan makes a list of every idea he has about volcanoes, then groups the ideas he likes best." Which stage of the writing process is Jordan in: planning, revising, or editing?

steps: Notice the words "before writing" and "makes a list of every idea." This happens before any drafting.
Gathering and grouping ideas before you write is part of planning (also called prewriting).
It is not revising or editing, because there is no draft yet to change or fix.
Answer: planning.

items.prompt: Read the action: "After finishing a draft, Maria fixes a misspelled word and adds a missing capital letter at the start of a sentence." Is this revising or editing?

steps: Fixing a misspelled word and adding a capital letter are surface corrections.
Editing means correcting conventions like spelling, capitalization, and punctuation without changing the ideas.
Maria did not change the content or organization, so this is not revising.
Answer: editing.

items.prompt: Read the action: "To improve her paragraph, Lena moves the last sentence to the beginning so the main idea comes first." Is this revising or editing?

steps: Moving a sentence to improve the order changes the organization of the ideas.
Revising means changing content, focus, or organization to make the writing stronger.
Lena did not fix spelling or punctuation, so this is not editing.
Answer: revising.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: "The soup was good and the bread was good." Which single word best replaces the repeated word "good" to make the sentence more precise: "nice," "delicious," or "fine"?

steps: The sentence repeats the weak, vague word "good."
"Delicious" is a precise word that clearly describes tasty food.
"Nice" and "fine" are still vague and do not add precision.
Answer: delicious.

items.prompt: Read the action: "In a finished draft, Sam adds commas where they were missing and corrects a run-on sentence." Is this revising or editing?

steps: Adding commas and fixing a run-on sentence are punctuation and grammar fixes.
Editing corrects surface conventions without changing the writer's meaning.
Sam did not change the ideas or organization, so this is not revising.
Answer: editing.

items.prompt: Read the action: "Before starting his essay, Theo draws a web with his topic in the center and supporting ideas branching off." Which stage of the writing process is this: planning, revising, or editing?

steps: The action happens "before starting his essay," so no draft exists yet.
Making a web or organizer to arrange ideas before drafting is planning.
It is not revising or editing, which both come after a draft is written.
Answer: planning.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: "my brother and i walk to school on monday." Which edited version corrects the capitalization without changing the meaning: "My brother and I walk to school on Monday." or "my brother and I walks to school on monday."?
items.answer: My brother and I walk to school on Monday.

steps: The original needs a capital M at the start, a capital I for the pronoun, and a capital M for Monday.
"My brother and I walk to school on Monday." fixes all three capitalization errors.
The other choice leaves "monday" lowercase and adds a verb error ("walks").
Answer: My brother and I walk to school on Monday.

items.prompt: Read the action: "Reading over her draft, Priya replaces the vague word 'thing' with the specific word 'telescope.'" Is this revising or editing?

steps: Replacing a vague word with a precise one improves word choice and clarity.
Revising includes changing words to make ideas clearer and more exact.
She did not fix a spelling or punctuation error, so this is not editing.
Answer: revising.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: "The car was very fast." Which single word best replaces "very fast" to make the sentence more precise: "quick," "speedy," or "race car"?

steps: The phrase "very fast" is wordy and vague.
"Speedy" is one precise adjective that replaces "very fast" cleanly: "The car was speedy."
"Quick" is weaker and less specific, and "race car" is a noun that does not fit the blank as a describing word.
Answer: speedy.

items.prompt: Read the action: "While drafting, a student wonders what to fix, so she rereads and adds a sentence giving a reason that supports her main idea." Is this revising or editing?

steps: Adding a supporting reason changes the content and develops the main idea.
Revising means improving content, focus, and support, not just surface fixes.
No spelling or punctuation was corrected, so this is not editing.
Answer: revising.

items.prompt: Read the action: "Before writing, Aiden decides his report will focus only on penguins, not all birds, so the topic is not too wide." Which stage is this: planning, revising, or editing?

steps: Choosing and narrowing a focused topic happens before drafting.
Selecting a focused topic is part of planning the writing.
There is no draft yet to revise or edit.
Answer: planning.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: "she dont like the cold weather." Which edited version corrects the errors without changing the meaning: "She doesn't like the cold weather." or "She do not likes the cold weather."?
items.answer: She doesn't like the cold weather.

steps: The original needs a capital S and the correct verb form.
"She doesn't like the cold weather." fixes the capital letter and uses the correct contraction and verb.
"She do not likes the cold weather." is still ungrammatical ("do not likes").
Answer: She doesn't like the cold weather.

items.prompt: Read the action: "A writer changes the spelling of 'freind' to 'friend' in her finished draft." Is this revising or editing?

steps: Correcting a spelling mistake is a surface convention fix.
Editing fixes spelling, capitalization, and punctuation without changing meaning.
The ideas and organization stay the same, so this is not revising.
Answer: editing.

items.prompt: Read the sentence: "The flowers were pretty and the flowers smelled pretty." Which single word best replaces the second "pretty" to make the sentence more precise: "nice," "sweet," or "good"?

steps: The sentence repeats the vague word "pretty" to describe a smell.
"Sweet" precisely describes a pleasant smell: "the flowers smelled sweet."
"Nice" and "good" are still vague and do not describe the smell exactly.
Answer: sweet.

items.prompt: Read the action: "After two tries fixing single words, readers still cannot follow a confusing paragraph, so the writer decides to rewrite the whole paragraph in a new way." Is this small editing or rewriting (trying a new approach)?

steps: The writer already tried changing single words twice, and it did not work.
When small fixes fail and readers still cannot follow the writing, the best step is to rewrite the section and try a new approach.
This is more than editing a convention; it is a major revision of the whole paragraph.
Answer: rewriting (trying a new approach).
